headline: Palladian Locks Up the Sky — Corponation Wins Atmospheric Processing Monopoly
body:
Palladian Corporation finalized a 50-year exclusive licensing agreement with the Federal Remnant's Environmental Continuity Office on Thursday, securing sole commercial rights to atmospheric processing operations across the entire Great Lakes Reclamation Zone — a jurisdictional area that encompasses GLMZ and eleven surrounding settlement clusters. The deal, valued at approximately 4.2 trillion quanta in projected revenue, grants Palladian control over the network of filtration towers, acid-rain neutralization rigs, and particulate scrubbers that roughly 40 million people depend on for breathable outdoor air. Competing bids from Helix Biosystems and a Zheng-Dao environmental subsidiary were withdrawn under circumstances three Federal Remnant officials have since described, off the record, as 'not entirely voluntary.'

Palladian CEO Constance Adler-Yuen, speaking from the company's headquarters tower in The Spires, called the agreement 'the logical culmination of three decades of environmental infrastructure investment.' Critics are less sanguine. The Collective issued a statement within hours of the announcement warning that Palladian now holds 'a literal monopoly on breathing' and calling for emergency nationalization hearings. Zheng-Dao released a terse single-sentence response: 'We are reviewing our options.' Industry observers read that as a prelude to litigation — or worse.

For residents of the Gray Zone and The Narrows, the news landed like a weight. Community organizer Fatou Reyes-Lindqvist told the Gray Zone Voice that her district's atmospheric processing fees have already tripled in the two years since Palladian absorbed the district's previous service provider. 'They don't hide what they're doing,' she said. 'They just do it slowly enough that you can't catch your breath — literally.' Environmental monitors recorded a 12% spike in particulate levels in the Old Harbor district last month, which Palladian attributed to legacy infrastructure rather than service decisions.
aftermath: Within six months, three independent atmospheric processing co-ops operating in The Underworld were forcibly shut down by Ironclad contractors acting on Palladian's behalf, triggering the first major Bore Rat–Palladian confrontations in the tunnel networks.
runner_relevance: The Palladian monopoly created layered runner demand across every faction. The Bore Rats contracted smugglers to move black-market atmospheric filter components into The Narrows and the Gray Zone communities priced out of Palladian's fee structure. Zheng-Dao quietly opened a bounty channel for sabotage contracts targeting Palladian processing infrastructure — deniable work paying 60,000–90,000 quanta per rig disruption. The Collective hired protection runners to secure their community filtration stations from Ironclad enforcement sweeps. Graycloaks offered premium rates for runners who could extract documentary evidence of the Federal Remnant deal's coercion — the kind of proof that could unwind the contract in court.
